page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.8xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 32 virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, fall into the bottom 10% tier, and single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 are similarly positioned. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression tests. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached reads and writes remains in the average range, though the Passmark memory score is weak.

Given its shared CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.n4.8xlarge offers a resource-dense configuration for multi-threaded workloads that do not require sustained peak single-core performance. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for parallelized tasks such as multi-threaded software compilation, image processing, and basic web serving. The lack of local storage and GPUs makes it suitable for workloads reliant on network-attached storage, such as distributed database operations, static web serving, and moderate-scale LLM inference.
